body.message: Can I afford to open a second shop?

body.reply:
Second-shop check (assumed: ৳6,00,000 set-up cost, ৳75,000/month extra rent and salaries):
• If total sales rise 25%: monthly profit ৳45,284 (now ৳50,497), lowest cash in 8 weeks -৳8,11,556.
• If sales rise only 10%: monthly profit ৳3,412, lowest cash -৳8,34,907.
• New break-even: about ৳6,94,360 of sales per month.
Verdict: not affordable right now. Opening would push cash below zero on top of the winter stock bills. Revisit after those bills are settled, or with financing in place.

body.message: Am I more profitable than similar shops?

body.reply:
Compared with 39 anonymised similar shops, you do better than about 43% of them overall.
• Gross margin: you 37.2% vs peer median 32.7% (better than 85%)
• Sales growth vs last year (12 weeks): you -0.5% vs peer median 6.8% (better than 26%)
• Rent + salaries + overheads as share of sales: you 24.5% vs peer median 22.4% (better than 33%)
• Overdue customer dues as share of monthly sales: you 9.4% vs peer median 4.0% (better than 13%)
• Cash buffer (weeks of spending): you 2.1 weeks vs peer median 4.3 weeks (better than 38%)
• Debt-service coverage (DSCR): you 1.94 vs peer median 1.23 (better than 63%)
→ Sales are growing slower than similar shops. Compare your best-selling lines and prices with the season's demand.
→ Your fixed costs are about ৳15,684 per month above what similar shops carry for the same sales. Rent and staffing are the usual places to look.
→ Bringing overdue dues down to the peer level would free about ৳40,299 of cash. Ask the agent to send reminders, and set a credit limit for repeat late payers.
